newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber up on Japan in dull trade.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber up on Japan in dull trade.

text.p: Prices in the Singapore rubber market were indicated higher by midsession on Wednesday because of higher prices in Japan, although trading remained dull and uninspiring, dealers said.
"Prices were marked up this morning largely because of the Japanese market. Otherwise, the consumers were stepping back and waiting for leads this afternoon," a dealer said.
Tokyo's benchmark October contract was up 1.2 yen to 141.0 while Kobe's October contract also gained 1.2 yen to 140.6.
"There were just no leads to speak of this morning. It was fairly dull," another dealer said.
Traders said they were hoping the active covering they saw on Tuesday will come up anew.
"But it's hard to tell in this market, especially when consumer demand is so weak," one dealer said.
At 0430 GMT, June RSS3 was indicated at 110.00-111.00 U.S. cents a kg from 109.50 cents.
June RSS1 was indicated at 159.00 Singapore cents (US$1.11) a kg from 158.25 cents. June TSR20 was indicated at 153.75 Singapore cents (US$1.07) a kg from 152.75 cents.
